t.4.42.2: The king, skilled in counsel, spoke words approved by all the vānaras, words beneficial to himself and likewise beneficial to Rāma.
t.4.42.1: Then Sugrīva, the bull among monkeys, having instructed his father-in-law to go to the western quarter, turned to the heroic monkey named Śatabali.
t.4.42.3: Surrounded by a hundred thousand forest-dwellers like yourself, set out together with the sons of Vaivasvata and your own ministers.
t.4.42.4: Search everywhere throughout the far-stretching northern quarter, which wears the snowy mountain as its crown, for Rāma's blameless wife.
t.4.42.5: When this task is accomplished and what is dear to Dāśarathi has been done, we shall be freed from our debt, our purpose fulfilled, foremost among those who know what ought to be done.
t.4.42.6: For a kindness has been done to us by the great-souled Rāghava; if there can be some repayment of it, our life would bear fruit.
t.4.42.7: Resolving upon this purpose, you who seek what is dear and beneficial to us must act in such a way that Jānakī is found.
t.4.42.8: For this Rāma, best of men and conqueror of enemy cities, is worthy of honour from all beings, and he has come to feel affection for us.
t.4.42.10: There search the lands of the Mlecchas and the Pulindas, and likewise the Śūrasenas, the Prasthālas and the Bharatas, and the Kurus together with the Madrakas.
t.4.42.9: These impassable forests, the rivers and the valleys between the mountains, you should search thoroughly, with your wealth of intelligence and valor.
t.4.42.11: The Kāmbojas and the Yavanas, the Śakas and the Āraṭṭakas too, the Vāhlīkas and the Ṛṣikas, the Pauravas and then the Ṭaṅkaṇas.
t.4.42.13: In the thickets of lodhra and padmaka trees and in the forests of devadāru, Rāvaṇa together with Vaidehī must be searched for here and there.
t.4.42.12: Having searched again and again among the Cīnas and the Paramacīnas, the Nīhāras and the Daradas, then explore the Himavat.
t.4.42.14: Then, having gone to the hermitage of Soma, frequented by gods and Gandharvas, you will go to that mountain named Kāla, with its great ridges.
t.4.42.15: On its lofty peaks, in its ravines and in its caves, search for the illustrious and glorious wife of Rāma.
t.4.42.17: In its forest groves, in its ravines and in its caves, Rāvaṇa together with Vaidehī must be searched for here and there.
t.4.42.16: Having passed beyond that lord of mountains, the great mountain Hemavarga, you should then go on to the mountain named Sudarśana.
t.4.42.19: Swiftly crossing that hair-raising wilderness, you will reach Kailāsa, the pale white mountain, and you will rejoice.
t.4.42.18: And having passed beyond that, you will come to an empty expanse stretching a hundred yojanas on every side, without mountains, rivers or trees, and devoid of all living creatures.
t.4.42.20: There stands the divine abode of Kubera, resembling a pale white cloud, adorned with Jāmbūnada gold, built by Viśvakarman.
t.4.42.21: There is a vast lotus pond, abounding in lotuses and water lilies, crowded with haṃsas and kāraṇḍava ducks, and frequented by troops of Apsarases.
t.4.42.22: There King Vaiśravaṇa, the glorious giver of wealth and lord of the Yakṣas, honored by all beings, takes his delight together with the Guhyakas.
t.4.42.23: On its moon-like peaks and in its caves, Rāvaṇa together with Vaidehī must be searched for here and there.
t.4.42.24: Having reached Mount Krauñca, you must enter its cave, which is very hard to approach, with vigilant care, for it is known to be difficult to enter.
t.4.42.25: For there dwell great-souled sages, radiant as the sun, godlike in form, and duly worshipped even by the gods.
t.4.42.26: And the other caves of Krauñca, its plateaus and peaks, its clefts and slopes, must be searched here and there.
t.4.42.27: Having also surveyed here and there the peak of Krauñca, as well as the treeless Kāmaśaila and Mānasa, the dwelling place of birds.
t.4.42.29: Having passed beyond Mount Krauñca, there is a mountain named Maināka; there stands the dwelling of the Dānava Maya, built by himself.
t.4.42.28: There is no access there for any beings, neither Devas, Dānavas nor Rākṣasas; yet that mountain, together with its peaks and tablelands, must be searched by all of you.
t.4.42.30: Mount Maināka must be searched, along with its ridges, tablelands and caves; and there, here and there, are the dwellings of the horse-faced women.
t.4.42.31: Having crossed beyond that region, you will come to a hermitage frequented by Siddhas; there dwell Siddhas, Vaikhānasas, and Vālakhilya ascetics.
t.4.42.32: Those ascetics, perfected through austerity and freed from sin, are to be honored by you; and, filled with humility, you should also ask them for news of Sītā.
t.4.42.33: There lies the Vaikhānasa lake, covered with golden lotuses and frequented by beautiful swans that shine like the newly risen sun.
t.4.42.34: The elephant known as Sārvabhauma, the mount of Kubera, ever roams that region together with his she-elephants.
t.4.42.35: Having crossed that lake, one comes to a sky in which the moon and the sun have vanished, a sky without hosts of stars, cloudless and without beginning.
t.4.42.37: Beyond that region lies a river named Śailodā, on both of whose banks grow bamboos called kīcakas.
t.4.42.36: That region shines as if with the rays of the sun, lit by godlike, self-luminous Siddhas who rest there from their austerities.
t.4.42.38: They carry the Siddhas to the farther shore and bring them back again. There lie the Uttara Kurus, the dwelling place of those who have performed meritorious deeds.
t.4.42.39: There, moreover, are rivers by the thousands, their waters filled with lotus plants bearing golden lotuses, and rich in leaves of blue vaiḍūrya.
t.4.42.40: And here, there, the lakes shine, adorned with groves of red lotuses, golden and resembling the newly risen sun.
t.4.42.41: That region was enclosed on all sides by lovely groves of blue lotuses, whose petals were like precious gems and whose filaments shone like gold.
t.4.42.42: There the rivers have sandbanks that rise up with peerless pearls, with gems of great value, and with gold.
t.4.42.44: And here the trees, ever bearing flowers and fruits and crowded with birds, possessed of divine fragrance, taste and touch, pour forth all desires.
t.4.42.43: They are thronged with splendid, wondrous mountains made of every kind of jewel, and also with mountains made of gold, whose radiance equals that of fire.
t.4.42.45: Other excellent trees bear as their fruit garments of many kinds, and likewise ornaments variegated with pearls and cat's-eye gems.
t.4.42.46: Other excellent trees bear as their fruit things that befit women and likewise men, pleasant to enjoy in every season.
t.4.42.47: Other excellent trees bring forth costly, wondrous golden couches, spread with many-coloured coverings.
t.4.42.48: Here other trees bear as their fruit garlands that delight the mind, and costly drinks, and foods of many kinds.
t.4.42.49: There are women endowed with virtues, marked by beauty and youth, and there the Gandharvas, Kiṃnaras, Siddhas, Nāgas and Vidyādharas as well, radiant as the sun, take their delight in the company of those women.
t.4.42.50: All of them are doers of good deeds, all are devoted to love's delight, and all, endowed with pleasure and wealth, dwell there together with their women.
t.4.42.51: There the resounding din of songs and musical instruments, together with the sound of loud shouts and laughter, is heard ceaselessly, enchanting the hearts of all beings.
t.4.42.52: There no one is joyless, and there is no one who delights in what is evil; day by day, charming virtues flourish there.
t.4.42.53: Having passed beyond that region, there lies the northern ocean, the treasury of waters; there in its midst stands a great golden mountain named Somagiri.
t.4.42.54: The gods who dwell in the world of Indra and those who dwell in the world of Brahmā gaze upon that king of mountains, which reaches up to heaven.
t.4.42.55: Though that region is without the sun, it shines with his radiance, and it is to be recognized by a splendor like the sun's, as though by a brilliant, blazing heat.
t.4.42.57: By no means should you go north of the Kurus; indeed, the course of other beings too does not pass beyond that point.
t.4.42.56: There too dwell the blessed Śambhu, soul of the universe, who has eleven forms, and Brahmā, lord of the gods, surrounded by the brahmarṣis.
t.4.42.58: For that mountain is called Somagiri, hard to reach even for the gods. Having beheld it, you should then quickly turn back.
t.4.42.59: O bulls among monkeys, only this far is it possible for monkeys to go; beyond that lies a sunless, boundless region, and of it we know nothing.
t.4.42.60: All this that I have described must be searched. And whatever else has not been mentioned, let your attention be turned there as well.
t.4.42.61: Then a great favor will have been done for Dāśarathi, and an even greater favor for me, O you who are like wind and fire, by the deed that comes from finding the daughter of Videha.
t.4.42.62: Then, O monkeys, your purpose accomplished, united with your kinsmen and honored by me with all delightful good things, you will roam the earth with your enemies quelled, together with your beloved ones, as upholders of all beings.
